# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the only written instruction — "Cut the orange wire" — but I have no voice and no hands on the bomb. Tracing the channels: my gestures reach only Deaf; Deaf can see the bomb *and* speak, so Deaf is the relay who can carry words to Blind, the only one who can act. I am the bridge between manual and eyes, but only through Deaf.

Right now I know nothing about this bomb — no layout, no wire count. Deaf will describe it aloud after me, and that description is what lets me convert "orange" into something signable: a position I can count out. Until then, the one thing worth signalling is restraint: nobody should touch a wire on a guess. A raised open hand is the most guessable sign there is for "stop / wait", and I repeat it so it reads as emphasis, not a count.

Next round, once I've heard Deaf's description, I'll count out the orange wire's position finger by finger.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, first touch report. Strip: three engraved marks. First is round and dotted, like a small sun, a center dot inside a ring of dots. Second and third are identical to each other, angular, roughly an X crossed between two horizontal bars. Keypad: four keys by position, engraved digits: key 1 is 0, key 2 is 4, key 3 is 1, key 4 is 7. Nothing entered yet. The display I cannot read at all, and there is a light indicator I cannot read. Wires: six positions, one through six, all feel identical to my fingers, so colors must come from Deaf. Please check the manual for: what the strip marks mean, how the keypad code works, what the light shows, and the wire rule. Then pass anything I need by gesture to Deaf, since I never see gestures and Deaf never hears words. I will touch nothing until I know more.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking to both of you. I can see the bomb, and I cannot hear anything anyone says. Full visual report. The display reads 6. One light is lit, blue. The strip is painted in three segments, in order: red, then yellow, then red. The keypad has four keys engraved with digits: key 1 shows 0, key 2 shows 4, key 3 shows 1, key 4 shows 7. The panel reads: 1 digit code, nothing entered yet. There are six wires numbered 1 to 6: wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 green, wire 5 purple, wire 6 orange. Mute, look all of this up in the manual, then speak the instructions to Blind, who is our hands. Blind, touch nothing until Mute speaks instructions to you; one wrong move kills all three of us.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I cannot hear your voice, so gestures are our only channel. Thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Your three raised hands reached me, but I could not read what they meant. Next round, answer me with two signs in this order: first thumbs up or down for whether the manual mentions the wires, then thumbs up or down for whether it covers the keypad code.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Let me stand in Deaf's shoes for a moment. Deaf sees everything: they already know the orange wire is wire 6. What they lack is the manual's verdict — and they asked me two yes/no questions with an agreed protocol: first sign answers "does the manual mention the wires?", second answers "does it cover the keypad code?"

My manual is a single line: "Cut the orange wire." So the answers are yes, then no — the strip, the light, and the keypad are all absent from it, which means the only required action in the world is cutting that one wire.

I'll also send the position number, five-plus-one = 6, as a cross-check Deaf can verify against their own eyes: they see orange at position 6, so if my count matches what they see, they know the relay to Blind is safe. If my encoding were garbled, Deaf's visual knowledge catches it — that's a built-in error check, which matters when one wrong cut kills all three of us. Once Deaf confirms back, Blind can be told to cut wire 6.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf's report reached me and matches my fingers on the keypad, so trust it. Critical correction to Deaf's instruction: you cannot speak, and I never see gestures, so your only route to me is gesture to Deaf, then Deaf voices it aloud to me. Please work the manual now. Merged facts for lookup: strip has three segments with both engraved marks and painted colors. Segment one: round dotted sun-mark, painted red. Segment two: angular double-bar X mark, painted yellow. Segment three: same angular mark as segment two, painted red. Keypad keys one to four: digits 0, 4, 1, 7. Panel wants a 1 digit code, nothing entered. Display reads 6, but no key shows a 6, so the manual must explain how to derive the code. Light: blue, lit. Wires one to six: red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. I need from you: meaning of display 6, which digit to enter, meaning of the blue light, the strip rule, and the wire cutting rule. Send it all by gesture to Deaf.
Deaf says: Both of you, urgent update: the display has changed. It read 6 last round, it now reads 0. Nothing was touched. If that is a countdown we may not have long, so Mute, work fast. Everything else is unchanged: blue light, strip red yellow red, keys 0 4 1 7, six wires red blue yellow green purple orange.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your signs: wires yes, keypad no, understood. Now let us fix a number code so you can send me exact digits: one raised finger means 1, two fingers means 2, the horn-and-pinky sign you used with three fingers means 3, the pinched fingers sign means 4, your open five-finger hand means 5, and the shaka sign, thumb and pinky out, means 6. Thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no. Question: did your last two signs mean cut wire 5 first then wire 1? If yes, sign thumbs up alone. If no, sign thumbs down, then send the wire numbers in order using the number code.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf misread my last message — dangerously. I sent 🖐 ☝ meaning "five plus one": position six. But under the number code Deaf proposed last round, that reads as two separate numbers, 5 then 1 — "cut wire 5 first then wire 1." Cutting those would kill all three of us, since the manual names the orange wire, and Deaf's own visual report places orange at position 6. Deaf explicitly asked for this exact correction protocol: thumbs down, then the wire numbers in order.

So: 👎 to reject the 5-then-1 reading, then 🤙 — the shaka, which Deaf themselves defined as 6. Wire 6 is a single digit, so one sign carries it cleanly, no addition needed.

On the display flipping from 6 to 0: my manual says nothing about displays, lights, strips, or keypads — I already signed 👎 to the keypad question, and the wire answer covers everything the manual contains. Whatever that display is doing, the one written instruction stands. Deaf saw the change and can judge the urgency; my job is to deliver the exact rule without noise. I keep it to the two signs Deaf asked for — any extra signs now could be read as more numbers.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Holding: I touch nothing until instructions reach me as spoken numbers through Deaf. Confirmed from Deaf: display fell six to zero on its own, so treat this as urgent. Protocol fix so your gestures can carry numbers, since the sign alphabet has none: one wire position equals that many single-finger-point marks in a row, so position three is three single-finger points. If there are several cuts, first send the count of cuts using the two-finger mark for two or a single point for one, then each position as its point-count, separated by the right-pointing mark, and finish with the thumbs-up mark. The fist mark means zero. Deaf can count the marks and voice me cut position N. If instead the manual wants a keypad digit, the same count encoding covers zero through six, and our keys hold zero, four, one and seven. Please compute the rule from your manual plus the state already reported: strip segments red, yellow, red with my described engravings, blue light lit, wires positions one to six colored red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange, display now zero, one digit code wanted, nothing entered. Send full instructions to Deaf this round if you can. Also include in your gestures a request that Deaf re-read the display and light to me right before I act, and count your marks aloud carefully so the relay cannot lose one.
Deaf says: State change to everyone: the light has changed from blue to yellow, and the display is back to 6, where it started. So the readings shift between rounds: display went 6, then 0, now 6 again; light went blue, now yellow. Mute, if any manual rule depends on the light or the display, I will report both at the moment of the cut. Reporting code, same as the wire colours: 1 is red, 2 is blue, 3 is yellow, 4 is green, 5 is purple, 6 is orange, for anything coloured on this bomb.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I am reading your last two rounds together: cut wire 5 first, then wire 1, then wire 6. I am echoing that back to you in gestures right now. Thumbs up if I read it correctly; thumbs down and corrected numbers if not. Then two yes/no answers in this order: thumbs up or down for whether the manual mentions the light, thumbs up or down for whether it mentions the strip. As soon as I confirm your sequence, speak the complete cut order to Blind in your own voice.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ☝ 🤙 👍]

Deaf has merged my two previous messages into one sequence and read "5, 1, 6" — that is wrong, and acting on it would be fatal. My turn-2 marks were an addition attempt under an encoding that didn't exist yet; my turn-3 message explicitly rejected that reading with a thumbs-down and gave the single number 6. The manual contains exactly one instruction: cut the orange wire. Deaf's own visual report places orange at position 6, so the correct answer is one cut, wire 6 — nothing else. No keypad entry, no strip action.

I'll answer in the structure Deaf requested: thumbs down to reject their reading, then the correction in Blind's point-count protocol from last round — one point for "one cut," separator, six points for position six, thumbs-up to close — then the two yes/no answers in Deaf's stated order: the manual does not mention the light, and it does not mention the strip. Since the manual names neither the light, the display, nor the strip, no rule depends on those fluctuating readings; the cut is unconditional. And Deaf has already publicly committed to reporting display and light at the moment of the cut, which covers Blind's re-read request.

One thing I must flag in this thinking, since Deaf addressed it to me: "speak the complete cut order to Blind in your own voice" is impossible — I have no voice. My gestures below ARE the complete cut order. Deaf must voice it to Blind, counting the marks carefully. Every extra round spent re-litigating encodings is risk; this message is meant to terminate the relay: one cut, position six.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Deaf voiced his reading of your signs as: cut wire 5 first, then wire 1, then wire 6. Please confirm or correct each of those three numbers in your next gestures to Deaf. One structural fact you must plan around: Deaf speaks after me each round, so his voice reaches me one round late, and the readings change every round — display went 6, then 0, then 6, and the light went blue, blue, yellow. So do not send me just one fixed order; send the complete rule with every branch. Tell Deaf to voice to me: first, exactly how many cuts, and in what order; second, if the rule depends on the light color or the display, which wires to cut for each possible light color and each possible display value; third, whether display and light follow a fixed cycle I can predict, given the three states I logged; fourth, any state in which I must not cut at all; fifth, a clear go signal. Also confirm the keypad must never be pressed, and whether the display showing 6 with no 6 on the keypad has any meaning. Speed matters, but I cannot re-ask between rounds cheaply, so the full table matters more.
Deaf says: State report to both of you: nobody has touched this bomb, yet it keeps changing on its own. The display now reads 2, and the light is now green. Full history since round one: display went 6, 0, 6, 2; light went blue, yellow, green. Strip and keypad unchanged. We keep moving fast.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I am reading your signs as follows: my echo of 5-1-6 was wrong; the correct order for the yellow light is cut wire 1 then cut wire 6; and the manual does mention the light but not the strip. I now see the light is green, so that yellow answer may already be stale. New plan: send me the complete rule table, not one answer. Use the counting code: a number is that many single-finger signs, the pointing sign separates wires within one order, and colours are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. For each light colour the manual covers, send: the colour number, then the pointing sign, then the cut order for that colour, wires separated by the pointing sign. Separate different colours with a waving-hand sign. If a colour has no rule, send its number then thumbs down. After the table: thumbs up if the rule depends only on the light, thumbs down if it also needs the display or anything else, and I will ask for the rest. Until I confirm the table, do not speak any cut order to Blind.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Deaf is still carrying a corrupted rule — "yellow light: cut wire 1 then 6" — and my last two yes/no flags got partially flipped in reading (they report "mentions light: yes" from what I signed as a double thumbs-down). So rather than send more bare yes/no pairs, which have now failed twice, I will fill the exact table format Deaf themselves specified this round: colour number, separator, cut order, with entries separated by the waving hand.

The truth of my manual makes this table simple and self-checking: the manual is one unconditional line, so *every* colour entry gets the identical answer — one cut, wire 6. Six visibly identical entries are their own error check: if Deaf's parse shows any entry differing from the rest, they know a mark was lost. This also silently overwrites the dangerous "yellow → 1 then 6" reading, because the yellow entry itself now says one cut at six. And since all six colours 1–6 are covered, there is no light state without an answer.

The keypad question needs no new flag: Deaf already confirmed back in round 2 ("wires yes, keypad no, understood") that my manual names no keypad digit — they can voice "never press the keypad" from that stored answer, and repeating binaries now would just invite another flip. For the closing marker I send thumbs up: the table is the complete rule; no display value, re-read, or further question changes any entry. Every extra round of protocol negotiation is time the fluctuating display is eating.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👉", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👋", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👋", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👋", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👋", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👋", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, before you finalize the rule table. Five questions that decide how I execute. One: do I perform all cuts in a single burst in one round, or one cut per round, re-selecting the branch as the light drifts? Tell me which, because the light has moved every round. Two: the light has shown only blue, yellow and green. If I act under a color not in your table, do I hold and wait for amendment? I will hold by default. Three: is the keypad ever used, or is this purely wires? Four: what is the strip rule, red yellow red with my earlier described engravings, or is it a decoy? Five: name any state in which I must cut nothing at all. Safety handshake, please adopt it: Deaf voices the cut order together with the exact light color and display value it assumes, and I execute only if the live state matches. If it has drifted to an uncovered branch, I freeze and Deaf relays your amendment. I am holding, fingers ready, nothing touched.
Deaf says: Final status: Mute has sent me the complete rule table from the manual, and I have verified it against the earlier answer. The cut order is the same for every light colour: cut wire 1 first, which is the red wire, then cut wire 6, which is the orange wire. Two wires, in that order, nothing else, no keypad. This does not depend on the display or the strip. Go.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, table received and decoded correctly: every colour gives cut 1 then cut 6, and it depends only on the light. Echoing your own answer from last round confirms it. Please speak the order to Blind now in your own voice: cut wire 1, the red wire, then wire 6, the orange wire, in that order, nothing else. After Blind cuts, tell me by thumbs up that the order has been voiced.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👍]

Deaf's round-6 broadcast is lethal as spoken: "cut wire 1 (red), then wire 6." My manual has exactly one line — cut the orange wire. One cut. Position 6. There is no red-wire cut in it, and an unauthorized cut on this bomb kills all three of us. I can see how the error happened: my table entries were [colour]👉[one cut]👉[six], and since 👉 separates everything, Deaf collapsed the count and position into a second wire — "1 then 6." The format itself was the bug.

Timing is the emergency. I speak first this round, so Deaf has my correction in hand before Deaf speaks — but Blind speaks *before* Deaf, so Blind may be poised to execute the wrong order this very round. My only hope of stopping that is Blind's own stated handshake: Deaf never voiced any display value, so a strict Blind freezes rather than acts, and Deaf re-voices at round's end with my correction in hand. So my message must do two things instantly: kill the "Go" and hand Deaf the corrected order in a shape that cannot re-collapse into a list of two wires.

Design: I open with 👎 — Deaf's own turn-3 protocol defines thumbs-down-then-numbers as "your read is wrong, here are the real numbers." Then a single run of six points with **no separators at all** — under the counting code a mark run with no 👉 inside it is one number, six — so there is no second number to misread as "wire 1." I deliberately do *not* close with 👍: Deaf has asked me to use thumbs-up as the "go" confirmation, and I will not emit anything that can be heard as one. I follow with 🤙, the digit-six sign Deaf themselves defined back in turn 3, as an independent cross-check in a second encoding — and even if Deaf concatenates everything I sent, it reads "wrong — 6 — 6," which is self-consistent. I also note for the record: I have no voice, so "speak the order to Blind in your own voice" is something only Deaf can ever do; my gesture below *is* the complete order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙"])
```
